title: Hoag's Object: a wheel within a wheel
caption: Hoag's Object, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A nearly perfect ring of hot, blue stars circles a round, yellow core of older stars in this face-on Hubble view of Hoag's Object, one of the most unusual galaxies known.

Most galaxies are spirals, ellipticals or irregular smudges. A ring like this, cleanly separated from its center by a dark gap, is rare, and astronomers are still not sure how Hoag's Object came to look this way. The gap may not be empty: it could hold star clusters too faint to show up here.

Look between the ring and the core at about the one o'clock position and you can spot a second, far more distant ring galaxy in the background, a small echo of the one in front. At about 120,000 light-years across, Hoag's Object is a little larger than our own Milky Way.

understand.summary: Hubble's WFPC2 camera combined three broad filters: infrared I band shown in red, visible V band in green and blue B band in blue.
understand.eye: The colors are close to natural: the blue ring is young, hot stars and the yellow core is older, cooler ones.
